title: Gideon and the Vector
premise: Ansel Ishikawa, a forensic actuary who investigates 'impossible' insurance claims on the dying colony of Meridian's Reach, discovers his own name on the manifest of the Vector, a colony ship that officially never launched. The manifest belongs to the Kestrel Line massacre, an event erased from every archive, and Ansel realizes he is one of the few survivors whose memory was deliberately rewritten. As he reconstructs the truth, he uncovers that the colony's ruling Consortium engineered the disaster to seize inheritance rights over the colonists' gene-banks, and that his forgotten family died holding the proof. Hunted by the Consortium's adjusters, Ansel finds an unlikely found family among the colony's last holdouts—a disgraced archivist, a child born after the erasure, and the Vector's surviving pilot—and together they broadcast the restored records before the Consortium can scrub the final archive. The massacre is proven, the stolen inheritances are returned to the descendants, and Ansel, finally visible, chooses to stay and rebuild rather than vanish again.
about_author: Wendell Winterbourne is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who spent eleven years investigating losses at sea before turning to fiction. They write slow-burning science fiction about paperwork, grief, and the people history tries to lose.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of Loss
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. On Meridian's Reach, Ansel audits a suspiciously perfect accident claim in a half-abandoned docking ring, establishing his method: numbers don't lie, people do. He notes the colony's population declining faster than any official record admits. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Cross-referencing decommissioned hulls, Ansel finds the Vector listed on a 40-year-old manifest—with his own name among the passengers. The file self-deletes minutes after he reads it. Emotional beat: vertigo; the floor of his identity gives way.

chapters.title: The Archivist in the Basement
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Seeking the only un-networked records on the colony, Ansel finds Odile Vann, a disgraced archivist living among physical tape archives the Consortium declared obsolete. She recognizes the Vector's registry prefix and goes pale. Emotional beat: first fragile alliance, two people who trust paper more than people.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembered
chapters.summary: POV Juno (introduced). Juno, a twelve-year-old born after the erasure, recites a lullaby she shouldn't know—fragments of Vector crew songs preserved in her grandmother's dementia. Ansel hears his mother's voice in the melody. Emotional beat: grief arriving sideways, through a stranger's child.

chapters.title: Adjustment Notice
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. A Consortium 'adjuster' named Corvane arrives to audit Ansel's audit—polite, immaculate, threatening. Ansel realizes his investigation has been flagged and that investigators who find too much are reassigned or disappear. Emotional beat: hunted stillness; the predator wears a suit.

chapters.title: Forty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: POV Odile. Flashback chapter through Odile's recovered tapes: the Vector launched illegally carrying dissident families, was destroyed in orbit, and the Consortium erased it by rewriting every descendant's records—including implanting false memories. Emotional beat: horror at how thoroughly a lie can be built.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel tests his own memories against physical evidence and finds seams: a scar with no incident report, a language he reads but never learned. He confronts the possibility that everything he loves about his past was installed. Emotional beat: identity crisis at its lowest point.

chapters.title: Holdouts
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Odile leads him to the Undercroft, where the colony's forgotten—aging crew descendants, undocumented workers, Juno's grandmother—live outside Consortium ledgers. Ansel recognizes faces from the Vector manifest. Emotional beat: warmth of found family beginning to form around shared erasure.

chapters.title: Inheritance Law Is a Weapon
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Decoding the Consortium's motive: the Vector carried proprietary gene-banks and land charters; by killing the passengers and erasing them, the Consortium inherited their claims. Every 'impossible accident' Ansel ever investigated was the same crime repeating. Emotional beat: cold fury—the pattern finally visible.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Corvane offers Ansel reinstatement, wealth, and a clean new identity if he surrenders the manifest fragment. He implies Ansel survived the Vector because he cooperated once before. Emotional beat: temptation and self-disgust; the question of who Ansel was at forty.

chapters.title: The Pilot's Log
chapters.summary: POV Sefa (introduced). Sefa Reyes, the Vector's junior pilot, now a drunk freighter captain, kept a hidden flight log proving the ship was scuttled by Consortium tugs. She agrees to testify—if they can reach the wreck itself. Emotional beat: guilt seeking redemption.

chapters.title: Scrub Cycle
chapters.summary: POV Juno. The Consortium begins wiping the Undercroft's residents ahead of the colony's final decommissioning. Juno watches her grandmother forget mid-sentence as a suppression field activates. Emotional beat: terror and urgency—the erasure isn't history, it's happening now.

chapters.title: Dead Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. The group steals a derelict tug and plots a course to the Vector's crash site in the colony's debris shoals, evading Consortium patrols. Ansel navigates by instinct he can't explain—muscle memory from a life he doesn't remember. Emotional beat: the past becoming an ally instead of a wound.

chapters.title: The Wreck of the Vector
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Inside the drifting hulk, Ansel walks corridors his body knows, finding the sealed records vault and the remains of those who stayed behind to protect it—including, he slowly understands, his parents. Emotional beat: mourning made physical; touching the exact shape of loss.

chapters.title: Black Box
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Recovering the flight recorder, Sefa relives her last command decision—she obeyed an order to seal compartments, saving herself while others drowned in vacuum. Her testimony will convict the Consortium and condemn her. Emotional beat: choosing truth over absolution.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Corvane's ships trap them in the debris field; the tug is crippled, the recorder damaged, and Odile takes a radiation dose buying time. Ansel realizes Corvane isn't trying to kill them—he wants them led somewhere. Emotional beat: dread of a trap closing.

chapters.title: The Second Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Odile. In the vault, they find the true prize: not just evidence of the massacre, but the original charter naming every passenger as shareholders of the colony itself. The Consortium didn't just murder—they committed inheritance fraud on a civilizational scale. Emotional beat: hope sharpening into strategy.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Climax part one: using the colony's ancient distress array, they transmit the charter and black box to every ship, station, and ledger within range. Corvane cuts the power; Ansel completes the upload on battery and blood, broadcasting his own name as witness. Emotional beat: defiant triumph at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Reckoning
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Climax part two: incoming ships answer—not rescuers, but independent insurers and rival interests who now smell the fraud. Corvane, exposed by his own chain of command, is 'adjusted' by the Consortium he served. Ansel refuses to feel satisfaction. Emotional beat: justice arriving hollow, and honestly so.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: POV Juno. Weeks later, claims hearings begin. Juno, as a post-erasure descendant, becomes the face of the restitution case; her grandmother's remembered lullabies are entered as evidence. The holdouts become heirs. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into standing—erased people made legible again.

chapters.title: Names on the Manifest
chapters.summary: POV Ansel. Ansel restores the Vector's passenger list to the public memorial wall, reading each name aloud—including his parents', and finally his own. He declines resettlement elsewhere. Emotional beat: quiet homecoming; visibility chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: What We Keep
chapters.summary: POV Ansel, coda. A year on, Meridian's Reach is small but growing again. Ansel teaches Juno investigative method; Odile rebuilds the archives; Sefa flies supply runs. Ansel opens a new case file—an impossible accident, of course—and smiles. Emotional beat: earned hope; family as the record that outlasts every erasure.
